subject: Geo strictness roll-forward question: EKG pilot routing exceptions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: EKG pilot - strict geo binding / no-fallback ask

Hi Naomi / Karthik,

Quick context: EKG Health wants to pilot a highly-restrictive routing policy for a regulatory workload. Their asks are:
- Region lock: All inference traffic must be served only from the us-east region (no cross-region routing).
- No-fallback: If the pinned model variant is unavailable in us-east, requests should fail rather than fall back to other variants/regions.
- Forced model selection: They require the quantized v1.2 variant (for validated privacy profile) to be the only served model.

They sent a short residency matrix (attached) and want to kick off the pilot in ~3 weeks. They said they have an internal compliance checkpoint that will not sign off without a strict no-fallback guarantee.

Questions for you:
1) Is this something we can support for a pilot without new infra work (short-term operational configuration)?
2) If not, what are the minimal engineering changes and timeline?
3) What are the operational risks and recommended guardrails? (SLA / error modes / monitoring)

I copied Hannah because product will need to decide whether to allow per-account no-fallback locks, and Karthik for infra/serving feasibility. I can forward their residency spreadsheet and compliance notes if you want it.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: EKG_residency_matrix.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:37:00Z
Subject: Re: EKG pilot - strict geo binding / no-fallback ask

Marissa / Naomi,

Short answer: we can _implement_ something that behaves like a no-fallback/region lock for a single account, but there are trade-offs and at least two distinct implementation paths:

Option A (fast, operational):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in us-east for the customer and a routing rule that only targets that pool. If pool is exhausted, requests will receive a capacity-exhausted error (maps to their no-fallback requirement).
- Work required: capacity reservation, routing rule config, and a one-off per-account policy flag.
- Risk: if we misestimate demand, customer experiences full outages; operational overhead to guarantee headroom.

Option B (longer-term, safer):
- Control-plane feature to pin account -> model_variant -> region and to disable fallback for that pin. This requires: changes to route resolution logic, explicit orchestration to prevent cross-region fallbacks, and audit logs.
- Work required: ~2-3 sprints (infra + control plane + console exposure) and add a feature flag.

Technical questions we need answered from EKG:
- Expected steady-state QPS and 95th/99th percentile concurrency (tokens/sec or requests/sec).
- Expected peak/flash traffic window and any burst tolerances.
- Are they open to a dedicated SLA (reserved throughput) vs. soft capacity?

Operational guardrails we should include:
- Automatic alerting + escalation playbook if capacity-util > 80% for > 5m.
- Audit events when route/pin is applied/changed.
- A contract clause that clarifies error modes (we return HTTP 503 / capacity error if no local capacity).

If they need the pilot in 3 weeks, Option A is probably the only realistic path unless we re-prioritize INF-4312 immediately. We also need legal to vet the contractual language.

I can scope the dedicated pool config and estimate cost if you confirm expected throughput.

- Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: EKG pilot - strict geo binding / no-fallback ask

Thanks Karthik — helpful framing. Per Marissa: EKG expects about 12 req/s steady and 80 req/s burst (short lived); payloads are small (2-4 short prompts), token rate low. They will not accept cross-region hosting. Pilot objective is compliance validation, not scale.

Action items I propose:
- Marissa: confirm the numbers above with John (EKG contact) and share any compliance redlines they gave.
- Karthik / Connor: please triage Option A feasibility (dedicated us-east pool + routing rule + explicit no-fallback policy) and estimate cost + time for a 3-week pilot. If Option A is impossible, we need a firm statement so we can push the timeline.
- Hannah / Legal: please review the draft exemption (attached) and advise on contract language for error modes and monitoring obligations.

I'll book a 30 minute sync tomorrow to decide go/no-go if we have Karthik's feasibility estimate by EOD.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: EKG pilot - strict geo binding / no-fallback ask

On Mon, Aug 30, 2026 at 15:02 Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll book a 30 minute sync tomorrow to decide go/no-go if we have Karthik's feasibility estimate by EOD.

Quick ops perspective after a fast review:

Checklist for Option A (dedicated pool + no-fallback):
- [ ] Capacity: reserve a small dedicated GPU pool in us-east (estimate: single A100 equivalent for stated load; will refine after Karthik's numbers).
- [ ] Routing: add per-account routing rule that targets the reserved pool and has a hard "no-fallback" flag.
- [ ] Control-plane: implement a per-account annotation (route_lock=true) so UI/automation knows not to reroute.
- [ ] Observability: enable per-route token/cost traces + alerts (>=80% utilization) and surface in console for the account.
- [ ] Audit & Evidence: enable event logging for route_lock changes and retain logs for 90 days for compliance evidence.
- [ ] Contract: require customer-signed acknowledgment that service may return capacity errors when exhausted. Legal to own exact wording.

Operational notes:
- The control-plane change can be done as a config-first rollout (no code change to runtime) if we treat this as a strict routing rule that resolves only to a named pool. That keeps risk minimal and fits a 2-week ops window for configuration + testing.
- If we need UI exposure or long-term lifecycle (clearing pool after pilot), that needs a small console/perm cleanup ticket.

I can provision the reserve pool and wire routing rules if Karthik confirms the resource estimate. Suggest we do an internal dry-run (faking exhaustion) to show EKG the failure mode.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
